source.title: Adelie penguin area-wide breeding population census, 1991, present.
source.institution: Palmer Station Antarctica LTER / National Science Foundation

aggregation.island_year_total: sum all numeric colony-level breeding-pair counts within island and census year
aggregation.duplicate_colony_rule: fail closed if the same study, island, colony and year appears more than once
aggregation.synchronized_primary_panel: years with valid totals for all five islands

derived_quantities.endpoint_fraction: last observed total / first observed positive total
derived_quantities.annual_growth: log1p(N_t) - log1p(N_t-1) for adjacent calendar years only
derived_quantities.pairwise_synchrony: Pearson correlation among island annual-growth series
derived_quantities.common_component: PC1 of island-standardized log1p abundance over synchronized years
derived_quantities.common_growth_sensitivity: for each island regress annual growth on the mean annual growth of the other four islands
derived_quantities.additive_decomposition: compare null, island-only, year-only and island+year OLS models on log1p abundance

hypotheses.L1_shared_regional_decline: The five nearby islands should share a dominant long-term temporal component because they experience the same regional marine climate forcing.
hypotheses.L2_local_response_heterogeneity: Despite shared forcing, annual growth sensitivity and terminal decline should differ among islands, consistent with island-specific breeding-habitat filters.
hypotheses.L3_extinction_as_local_endpoint: Litchfield local extinction should appear as an extreme local endpoint rather than implying synchronous extinction across all islands.
hypotheses.L4_no_mechanism_yet: Synchrony and residual heterogeneity identify the scale of variation but do not by themselves establish sea ice, snow, geomorphology or competition as causes.

primary_outputs: island endpoint fractions and extinction years
pairwise annual-growth correlation matrix and median correlation
PC1 variance explained and island loadings
leave-one-island-out common-growth beta, R2 and residual SD
unique year, unique island and residual fractions from additive log1p decomposition
interpretation_boundaries: Do not call the year effect a causal sea-ice effect until sea-ice data are joined prospectively.
Do not interpret island residuals as competition; they may reflect geomorphology, snow, colony structure or observation noise.
Do not treat post-extinction zeros as evidence of continued demographic response after local extinction.
The five islands are neighboring breeding patches under shared regional ocean forcing, not independent biogeographic regions.
next_gate: After this synchrony result is frozen, define a mechanism contract before joining sea-ice and island physical-habitat predictors.
